type: the level as the running game holds it, read from MEM1: every placement record's state (+0x54), actor (+0xF4) and current position (+0x3C), and the placement instances the game created at run time, found by their class pointer 0x80481674 outside the resident section and paired with their template by model (+0xDC) and script (+0xA8)
structure: The resident object section is found by searching MEM1 for a placed record's stored position triple (floats are not rewritten by the loader) and checking a second placement (Mining at 0x80DC6F48, the tutorial at 0x80DBC020). In it, at the first playable frame of Mining: 60 records active with an actor, 313 dormant (state 2, no actor yet), 8 finished initialisers (state 3), 236 templates (state 5); 3 records moved by more than half a unit, none rewritten. Outside it, 276 words equal the placement class pointer; keeping the sane states and either a template pairing or a live actor away from the origin leaves 42 created instances, 11 of them paired with a template: two mining helmets on Molekins, the key at the key spawner, the stone art of two push blocks at their controllers, the cannon top and bottom at Push_Block_Template(13)'s position (-25.9, 0.1, -79.2), a button, the food dummy at the cannon barrel marker, the mining pick at its spawner, the fan blades on the fan. A clone's +0x5C points at its template again, not at its creator.

location.file_pattern: MEM1 while an editor-owned run is playing; .local/dolphin-evidence/scene-snapshots/<level>/*.json
location.offset: resident section base found at run time; instances at +0x00 class, +0x24 position, +0x3C current position, +0x4C heading, +0x54 state, +0xA8 script, +0xDC model, +0xF4 actor

meaning: This is how the editor shows the game's own view without running the scripts: a snapshot taken from Dolphin says which objects exist at that moment, where they stand, and which objects a script created and from which template. The objects the user saw missing on Mining (cannon, push-block art, fan blades, pick, key) are those created instances; the objects that looked absent in game are dormant records the game activates by distance. A snapshot is evidence about one moment of one run, LIKELY, and never a property of the file: the view draws it as an overlay (active solid, dormant dimmed, templates and finished hidden, moved records and clones at their in-game position) and nothing about it is saved or patched. Not covered: the creator of a clone (unknown pointer), actors without a model (the Skylander, cameras), and moments other than the one captured; CONFIRMED needs the same reads on a second boot and a second level.
